chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man whose slippers were destroyed and he was not able to find two slippers, he (peace be upon him) said: Let him wear the two socks (khuffayn) if he is compelled to do so, and let him tear them from the top of the foot; and if he wears the tilasan (a sleeveless garment), let him not button it on; so if he is compelled to wear a qaba (a long coat) due to cold, and he cannot find a garment other than it, let him wear it inside out, and let him not put his hands into the sleeves of the qaba.

key_terms.قَبَاءٍ: qaba (a long, often sleeveless or short-sleeved coat)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim in Ihram wear if they are forced to wear stitched clothing or socks due to necessity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific protocols for a pilgrim in Ihram who faces necessity (darura) to wear stitched garments or socks, emphasizing that the prohibition is lifted only when truly compelled. It prescribes practical modifications, such as tearing the top of the socks or wearing the coat inside out without sleeves, to mitigate the specific element of restriction (qabd) associated with stitched clothing. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition of stitched clothing is not absolute but conditional upon the absence of necessity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man whose slippers were destroyed and he was not able upon the slippers’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For him is that he should wear two shoes when he is desperate to that, and let him tear these from the back of the feet; and if he wears the pillion, so he should not button upon it. So if he was desperate to a robe due to cold, and he cannot find a cloth other than it, so let him wear it overturned, and he should not enter his hand in the sleeve of the robe’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man whose sandals were destroyed and was not able to find one, said, ’He can use a shoe in an emergency. He can tear its back for an opening and if he wears a shawl he must not button it. If one needs to use a Qaba 5 (a long coat) because of cold and cannot find other cloths he must wear it upside down and must not wear its sleeves on his arms.’”
